 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 21/04/2023
ORAL JUDGMENT
Since respondent No.3 has expired, case against the respondent No.3 is abated.

1. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of acquittal dated 22.10.2008 passed by the learned Principal District Judge, Junagadh in Sessions Case No.29 of R/CR.A/1181/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 2007, whereby the respondent accused came to be acquitted for the offences under section 306, 498(A), 114 of Indian Penal Code, the appellant - State Of Gujarat vs Bavkubhai Hadabhai Basia on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55122334/
1

sentences.text:
State has preferred present appeal under section 378 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code"
for short).

2. Brief facts of the complaint as per complainant is such that the complainant Sureshbhai lodged a complaint on 30.1.2007 to the effect that he is doing agricultural work and his younger sister Kanchanben married in the year 2002 with respondent No.3 and respondent Nos.1 and 2 are the in-laws of Kanchanben.
It is further the case of the prosecution that after marriage, Kanchanben started living in joint family at village Khamdhol.

After after 4-5 months of the marriage,
Kanchanben was keeping well at her matrimonial house.

But after six months, when Kanchanben came to her parental house, she told her parents that the respondent No.3 started beating her after drinking liquor and harassing her by saying that she was not liked by him.
Her in-laws also used to taunt her by saying her to go to her parental home.
But, after persuasion, Kanchanben again sent back to her matrimonial home by her parents.
After three months, respondent No.3 left Kanchanben at her parental home and thereafter, Kanchanben stayed at her parental home for about three years.
Before the date of incident, again Kanchanben was sent back to her matrimonial home on arriving at a compromise.

During that period, the complainant received telephonic message from her in-laws demanding Rs.50,000/- for purchasing an autorickshaw and threat was given if the same was not given, Kanchanben would remain no more.

On the day R/CR.A/1181/2009 JUDGMENT DATED:
21/04/2023 of incident, the complainant received message that her sister Kanchanben was burnt and died.
Thus, FIR being C.R.No.I-16 of 2007 came to be registered against the respondents accused for the aforesaid offences.

3. In pursuance of the complaint being C.R.No.I-16 of 2007 lodged by the complainant with the Junagadh Taluka Police Station for the aforesaid offences, the investigating agency recorded statements of the witnesses, drawn panchnama of scene of offence, discovery and recovery of weapons and obtained FSL report for the purpose of proving the offence.
After having found sufficient material against the respondents accused, charge-sheet came to be filed in the Court of concerned learned JMFC.
As said Court lacks jurisdiction to try the offence, it committed the case to the Sessions Court, Junagadh as provided under section 209 of the Code.
4. Upon committal of the case to the Sessions Court, Junagadh, learned Sessions Judge framed charge against the respondents accused for the aforesaid offences.
The respondents accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

5. In order to bring home charge, the prosecution has examined 14 witnesses and also produced various documentary evidence before the learned Sessions Court, more particularly described in para 2 of the impugned judgment and order.

6. On conclusion of evidence on the part of the prosecution, the Sessions Court put various incriminating circumstances appearing in the evidence to the respondents accused so as to obtain explanation/answer as provided u/s 313 of the Code.

In R/CR.A/1181/2009 JUDGMENT DATED:
21/04/2023 the further statement, the respondents accused denied all incriminating circumstances State Of Gujarat vs Bavkubhai Hadabhai Basia on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55122334/
2 appearing against them as false and further stated that they are innocent and false case has been filed against them.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have heard learned APP Mr. Shah for the appellant - State and and have minutely examined the record and proceedings provided to us during the course of hearing.
Learned APP would submit that the prosecution case is supported by PW 8,9,10,30,32 and 33.

Learned APP would further submit that considering the aforementioned witnesses, case against the present respondents accused are proved beyond reasonable doubt and therefore, present criminal appeal may be allowed.

8. We have heard learned APP appearing for the appellant State as well as learned advocate Mr.
Param Buch for the respondents and have minutely examined the documentary evidence provided to us by learned APP during the course of hearing.

9. On perusal of the evidence recorded before the learned Sessions Court, keeping in mind the charge framed against the accused more particularly, accused Nos.1 and 2, there is allegation of normal wear and tear of the married life and it does not attract concept of cruelty envisaged u/s 498A of the IPC and it does not affect u/s 306 of the IPC.
The allegations of harassment levelled against the accused are general in nature and none of this are sufficient to drive the victim leading to commit suicide.

The elements which are stated in the evidence of various witnesses for pointing out harassment in fact are not R/CR.A/1181/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 of such nature that which is likely to drive the victim to commit suicide.

Therefore, it appears that the learned Sessions Court has rightly passed order, which is well reasoned and has rightly assessed the evidence on record and found that no offence u/s 498A or 306 of the IPC is made out.
It is rightly observed that ingredients of section 107 of the IPC which is basic for abetment is also missing.
Learned APP is failed to point out any evidence which is left from being appreciated by the learned Sessions Court.

Under the circumstances, the learned Sessions Judge has rightly acquitted the respondents - accused upon elaborate reasons stated in the impugned judgment and we endorse the view/finding of the learned Sessions Judge leading to the acquittal.

10. It is a cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence that in an acquittal appeal if other view is possible, then also, the appellate Court cannot substitute its own view by reversing the acquittal into conviction, unless the findings of the Sessions Court are perverse, contrary to the material on record, palpably wrong, manifestly erroneous or demonstrably unsustainable.
(Ramesh Babulal Doshi V. State of Gujarat (1996) 9 SCC 225).

entities.text: Ramesh Babulal Doshi V. State of Gujarat (1996) 9 SCC 225
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the learned APP for the applicant has not been able to point out to us as to how the findings recorded by the learned Sessions Court are perverse, contrary to material on record, palpably wrong, manifestly erroneous or demonstrably unsustainable.

11. In the case of Ram Kumar v. State of Haryana, reported in AIR 1995 SC 280, Supreme Court has held as under:
"The powers of the High Court in an appeal from order of R/CR.A/1181/2009 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 acquittal to reassess the evidence and reach its own conclusions under Sections 378 and 379, Cr.P.C. are as extensive as in any State Of Gujarat vs Bavkubhai Hadabhai Basia on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55122334/
3 appeal against the order of conviction.

entities.text: Ram Kumar v. State of Haryana, reported in AIR 1995 SC 280
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State Of Gujarat vs Bavkubhai Hadabhai Basia
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But as a rule of prudence, it is desirable that the High Court should give proper weight and consideration to the view of the Trial Court with regard to the credibility of the witness, the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused, the right of the accused to the benefit of any doubt and the slowness of appellate Court in justifying a finding of fact arrived at by a Judge who had the advantage of seeing the witness.

It is settled law that if the main grounds on which the lower Court has based its order acquitting the accused are reasonable and plausible, and the same cannot entirely and effectively be dislodged or demolished,
the High Court should not disturb the order of acquittal."
12.

As observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajesh Singh & Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh reported in (2011) 11 SCC 444 and in the case of Bhaiyamiyan Alias Jardar Khan and Another vs. State of Madhya Pradesh reported in (2011) 6 SCC 394, while dealing with the judgment of acquittal

entities.text: Rajesh Singh & Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh reported in (2011) 11 SCC 444
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Bhaiyamiyan Alias Jardar Khan and Another vs. State of Madhya Pradesh reported in (2011) 6 SCC 394
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , unless reasoning by the learned Sessions Court is found to be perverse, the acquittal cannot be upset.

It is further observed that High Court's interference in such appeal in somewhat circumscribed and if the view taken by the learned Sessions Court is possible on the evidence, the High Court should stay its hands and not interfere in the matter in the belief that if it had been the Sessions Court, it might have taken a different view.
13.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court while considering the scope of appeal under Section 378 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, no case is made out to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.
In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, present Criminal Appeal deserves to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.

(J. C. DOSHI,J) SHEKHAR P. BARVE State Of Gujarat vs Bavkubhai Hadabhai Basia on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55122334/
